problem: allocate() calls _ref.allocate(amount, weights, 2), so the places argument is ignored: any places other than 2 either silently returns amounts at the wrong precision (places=0 gives [3.34, 3.33, 3.33] instead of [4, 3, 3]) or wrongly raises, and invalid places values (-1, True, 'x', 2.0) that main rejected with ValueError are now silently accepted.

Production code now imports and delegates everything to reference_impl, so any check that compares allocate against reference_impl compares the code with itself and can never fail, and importing allocate fails wherever reference_impl isn't shipped or a different module of that name comes first on sys.path.
_to_decimal is no longer called anywhere and is a verbatim copy of reference_impl.py:5-12, so it is duplicated dead code that makes the module look as if it still checks its inputs.
from fractions import Fraction is now unused (ruff F401), and Decimal on line 1 is used only by the dead _to_decimal.
The local reference_impl import sits in the same block as the standard-library imports with no blank line between the groups, contrary to PEP 8 import grouping.
